extra.message: protobuf-java and protobuf-javalite 3.21.x before 3.21.7, 3.20.x before 3.20.3, 3.19.x before 3.19.6, 3.16.x before 3.16.3 are vulnerable to a Denial of Service (DoS) attack through specially crafted input messages. It is recommended to upgrade protobuf-java and protobuf-javalite 3.21.x to 3.21.7, 3.20.x to 3.20.3, 3.19.x to 3.19.6, and 3.16.x to 3.16.3.

extra.message: A Affected versions of com.google.protobuf:protobuf-java and com.google.protobuf:protobuf-javalite are vulnerable to Uncontrolled Resource Consumption. The vulnerability stems from a parsing issue in the Message-Type Extensions, affecting certain package versions and allowing for Denial of Service (DoS) attacks through inputs containing multiple instances of non-repeated embedded messages with repeated or unknown fields; exploiting it triggers conversions between mutable and immutable forms, potentially leading to extended garbage collection pauses.

extra.message: Affected versions of com.google.protobuf:protobuf-java and com.google.protobuf:protobuf-kotlin are vulnerable to Incorrect Behavior Order. Parsing of unknown fields in the Java Protobuf runtime can be abused by a crafted binary payload (~800 KB) to trigger excessive short-lived object allocations, causing repeated GC pauses and prolonged parsing times, resulting in a Denial of Service.

metadata.sca-reachable-if: you deserialize untrusted protobuf data into a class of any of your Java protobuf packages, using a function such as `parseFrom(...)`
